sections.h2: What is Talbot County, Georgia, like?
sections.html:
Quiet and hilly. Talbot County takes up 395 square miles of west central Georgia, 391 of them land, and Talbotton holds the courthouse. Wikipedia records the county's founding on December 14, 1827 and its naming for Matthew Talbot.

The fall line cuts across the county. Ridges of the Pine Mountain range push past 1,000 feet in the far north, while the south is flatter and carries the Fall Line Freeway along State Route 96 between Geneva and Junction City. U.S. 80 and State Route 22 cross it too, and trains run on a CSX subdivision and the Norfolk Southern Columbus District.

Besides Talbotton, the municipalities are Woodland, Geneva and Junction City, and a piece of Manchester reaches in. Box Springs is a census-designated place, while Po Biddy Crossroads, Tax Crossroads and Centerville are unincorporated names that turn up on deeds. The mid-2025 estimate is 5,709 residents, about 15 per square mile.

sections.h2: What do Talbot County's housing and income figures show?
sections.html:
Most occupied homes here belong to the people living in them, 79.6% by the Census count, and the midpoint value of such homes is $117,100 for 2020-2024. Renters face a midpoint gross rent of $816.

No permits at all in 2025 and a commute of almost 43 minutes paint a county where people live here and drive elsewhere for work, and where nobody is adding houses. Nearly three in ten residents are past 65, so estates often put houses up for sale, and an heir meets the tax office before a buyer ever signs.

sections.h2: Where do Talbot County tax questions get answered?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner works from 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton and receives letters at P.O. Box 147. The office website lists weekday service from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, a noon closure, and phones at 706-665-3240 and 706-665-3280.

  • Tax commissioner: billing, collections, mobile home titles, timber tax, tax sales.
  • Tax assessors at 706-665-3377: value, returns, exemptions, appeal paperwork.
  • Commissioners' office, 35 Madison St., 706-665-3220: mobile home location permits.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: intangible tax on recorded loan documents.

Accepted forms of payment are cash, checks, money orders and Visa, MasterCard or Discover cards, and card payments carry an added fee. Look up a parcel through qPublic.

sections.h2: What is the Talbot County billing calendar?
sections.html:
Real and personal property statements typically arrive in October and fall due December 20. Part-payments are welcome. After the deadline, interest accrues at prime plus 3%, and every 120 days a further 5% penalty is added until the total hits 20%.

Mobile and manufactured homes follow a January-to-April rhythm. Statements usually go out early in the year with an April 1 deadline, a decal is handed over once the tax is paid, and the return for a home in the county on January 1 is also due April 1. Filing late costs a 10% penalty.

The tax office's site also carries a note about trash service: beginning January 1, 2026, the garbage collection fee is $225.00 per year, with extra carts at $137.00 per year. Ask the office whether that charge rides on your parcel's account so the closing agent includes it.

sections.h2: How is timber taxed in Talbot County?
sections.html:
Standing trees escape tax until sold or cut, and then 100 percent of fair market value is multiplied by the millage rate. The commissioner's page sorts these events into three kinds.

  • Lump sum sale: the purchaser fills out form PT-283T and delivers form and tax to the commissioner inside five business days, and is personally liable if the seller fails to pay.
  • Unit price sale: a quarterly report goes to the seller and the assessors 45 days after each quarter closes.
  • Owner harvest: the landowner reports to the assessors 45 days after the quarter and pays the tax.

If you have cut or plan to cut trees, ask the office whether a timber account is open before you list.

sections.h2: How does Talbot County auction property for unpaid tax?
sections.html:
The commissioner runs levy sales under Title 48 and Title 9 of the Georgia code. A parcel is advertised in the Talbotton New Era for four straight weeks, then auctioned on the first Tuesday of the month after the notices end.

  • Location and time: the courthouse on South Washington Avenue, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • The county gives no title guarantee, and the bidder gets no access to the property and no rent for at least a year.
  • The high bidder pays in cash or certified funds as soon as the sale ends.
  • Money left after taxes and costs becomes excess funds, claimed by written request to 38 South Jefferson Avenue.

The commissioner's site posts a guide to the right of redemption. An owner in arrears has time before the auction, and settling the account in a private sale may leave more equity with the seller.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a value or claim an exemption in Talbot County?
sections.html:
Both go through the tax assessors. A disputed value starts with a written filing to the Board of Assessors that names the route you want: Board of Equalization, Superior Court, arbitration, or hearing officer. The revenue department's county sheet sets the cutoff as a postmark no later than 45 days after the notice was mailed.

A real estate return is due between January 1 and April 1 whenever something changed, and omitting a required one costs 10% of the unreported value. Personal property returns, form PT-50P, are filed yearly by April 1.

For exemptions, April 1 is the cutoff the commissioner's site gives for the current year, and later filings roll to the next. The state sheet lists no local homestead exemption for Talbot, which leaves the statewide ones. An approved exemption renews itself until the owner moves or ownership changes.

sections.h2: What should a Talbot County seller do about unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Request a written payoff for each year still open, adding mobile home and timber accounts where they exist. With an inherited house, learn which years went unpaid before you list, since a recorded lien has to be paid at the table.

Refunds are narrow. A written request for tax paid in error goes to the Board of Commissioners within three years, and the commissioner's page ties refunds to errors of fault, not to a quarrel over value. Dividing the year's bill between buyer and seller happens on the settlement statement.

With so little building and a small buyer pool, a house with a tax cloud is harder to place. A cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands can pay the balance out of your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: What is the Talbot County tax commissioner's address?
faqs.a: 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton, with P.O. Box 147 for mail. Weekday service runs 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, with a closure from noon to 1:00.

faqs.q: When are Talbot County property tax bills due?
faqs.a: December 20 for real and personal property, with statements typically mailed in October. Mobile home bills fall due April 1.

faqs.q: Does Talbot County accept partial tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, the commissioner's property tax page says so. Interest and penalties still build on the remainder after the due date.

faqs.q: When do Talbot County tax levy sales happen?
faqs.a: They take place on a first Tuesday, once four weeks of Talbotton New Era notices have run, at the courthouse on South Washington Avenue between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the Talbot County homestead exemption cutoff?
faqs.a: April 1 for the current billing year. Per the commissioner's FAQ, forms are accepted all year, and a later one applies to the following year.
